earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: JPMorgan disclosed that its 2026 DFAST results are hypothetical supervisory stress estimates, not management forecasts of actual performance or capital ratios.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: The DFAST exhibit is a regulatory stress-test disclosure rather than forward-looking operating guidance.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: The results represent hypothetical estimates under the Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario prescribed by the Federal Reserve on February 4, 2026 and do not represent JPMorganChase's forecasts of actual expected gains, losses, pre-provision net revenue ("PPNR"), net income before taxes, capital, risk-weighted assets (“RWA”), or capital ratios.
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Important framing: DFAST outputs should not be treated as company guidance.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: The Federal Reserve kept JPMorgan's Stress Capital Buffer requirement unchanged through September 30, 2027, with new requirements to be calculated in 2027 under revised supervisory models.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: SCB requirements for large banks including JPM remain at current levels through September 2027.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: In February 2026, the Federal Reserve announced that the Stress Capital Buffer (“SCB”) requirements for large banks, including JPMorganChase, will remain at current levels through September 30, 2027 with new requirements to be calculated in 2027 based on revised supervisory models that incorporate public feedback.
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Provides near-term regulatory capital requirement visibility, though the filing says it does not disclose the firm's 2026 SCB requirement.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: Under the severe stress scenario, JPMorgan's projected minimum CET1 ratio is 12.4%, down from an actual 14.6% in 4Q25, indicating a 220 bp stressed drawdown while remaining above double digits.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: JPM's stress-test capital depletion leaves projected minimum CET1 at 12.4%.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: Actual 4Q25 Projected 1Q28 Projected Minimum2 Common equity tier 1 capital ratio (%) 14.6% 14.4% 12.4%
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Stressed minimum is within JPMorgan-run DFAST methodology and may differ from Federal Reserve-published results.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: JPMorgan's other stressed regulatory capital ratios also remain above their actual-period lows, with projected minimum Tier 1 risk-based capital of 13.3%, total risk-based capital of 15.3%, Tier 1 leverage of 6.2%, and SLR of 5.3%.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: JPM discloses stressed capital and leverage ratios that remain materially positive in the severe scenario.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio (%) 15.5% 15.3% 13.3% Total risk-based capital ratio (%) 17.4% 17.5% 15.3% Tier 1 leverage ratio (%) 6.9% 6.9% 6.2% Supplementary leverage ratio (%) 5.8% 5.8% 5.3%
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Shows stressed capital and leverage ratio floors under the supervisory severely adverse scenario.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: Projected standardized RWA rises from $1.982 trillion in 4Q25 to $2.089 trillion by 1Q28 under the severe scenario, increasing capital intensity by roughly $107 billion.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: Stress scenario assumptions increase JPM's projected RWA base.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: Actual 4Q25 Projected 1Q28 Basel III Standardized RWA ($B) $1,982 $2,089
earnings_release_evidence.notes: RWA expansion affects capital ratios during the stress horizon.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: In the nine-quarter stress horizon, JPMorgan projects $135.9 billion of PPNR but only $11.4 billion of net income before taxes after credit provisions, trading/counterparty losses, and other losses.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: Stress-test P&L shows strong PPNR but heavy loss absorption over nine quarters.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: Billions of dollars Pre-provision net revenue $135.9 2.9 % equals Net interest income 235.2 5.1 Noninterest income2 136.2 2.9 less Noninterest expense3 235.5 5.1 Other revenue4 0.0 less Provision for credit losses5 95.6 Credit losses on investment securities (AFS/HTM)6 0.2 Trading and counterparty losses7 10.9 Other losses/(gains)8 17.8 equals Net income before taxes $11.4 0.2 %
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Highlights stress profitability: substantial PPNR absorbs large loss assumptions, leaving positive pre-tax income.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: Projected credit-loss provisioning is the largest stress P&L drag at $95.6 billion over nine quarters, with $10.9 billion of trading and counterparty losses and $17.8 billion of other losses/gains.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: Loss assumptions materially reduce JPM's stress-scenario earnings.
earnings_release_evidence.excerpt: less Provision for credit losses5 95.6 Credit losses on investment securities (AFS/HTM)6 0.2 Trading and counterparty losses7 10.9 Other losses/(gains)8 17.8 equals Net income before taxes $11.4 0.2 %
earnings_release_evidence.notes: Stress scenario embeds material credit and market/counterparty loss assumptions.

earnings_release_evidence.title: 8-K earnings-release exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
earnings_release_evidence.claim: JPMorgan projects total loan losses of $70.2 billion and a 5.0% portfolio loss rate over the nine-quarter severe scenario, with credit cards and commercial & industrial lending among the largest disclosed loss categories.
earnings_release_evidence.summary: DFAST loan-loss projections show significant cumulative credit losses under severe stress.
